answer: Submissions that land within 239 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The meadow detector writes to zephyr, and garden shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 11 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 21 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
